name: Frujai Soldier
body:
FRUJAI SOLDIER
CR 12

XP 19,200
N Large plant
Init +2; Senses low-light vision; Perception +22

DEFENSE

AC 27, touch 11, flat-footed 25 (–1 size, +2 Dex, +16 natural)
hp 161 (17d8+85)
Fort +15, Ref +9, Will +9
Defensive Abilities absolute gravity; Immune plant traits

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., climb 20 ft.
Melee bite +21 (2d6+9 B&P&S), 2 talons +20 (1d6+9 P)
Ranged gravity anchor +14 touch (6d8 force plus reposition or trip, max. 150 ft.)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Special Attacks colony guard

STATISTICS

Str 28 (+9), Dex 15 (+2), Con 20 (+5), Int 8 (–1), Wis 15 (+2), Cha 14 (+2)
Base Atk +13; CMB +22; CMD 34 (38 vs. bull rush, reposition, or trip)
Feats Combat Reflexes, Improved Natural Attack (bite), Iron Will, Lightning Reflexes, Nimble Moves, Power Attack, Skill Focus (Perception, Stealth), Weapon Focus (bite)
Skills Climb +17, Perception +22, Stealth +19; Species Modifiers +4 Perception, +4 Stealth
Languages Frujai; telepathy 100 ft.

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Absolute Gravity (Su)

See above.

Colony Guard (Ex)

Whenever a frujai colony takes damage, all frujai soldiers within 300 feet gain a +4 morale bonus to attack rolls and a 10-foot bonus to their base speed for 1 round.

Gravity Anchor (Su)

A frujai soldier can create violent fluctuations in gravity as a ranged touch attack with a 150-foot range and no range increment. If the attack hits, the soldier can attempt either a reposition or a trip combat maneuver against the target as a free action, gaining a +4 bonus to perform the maneuver. When repositioning a creature in this way, the frujai soldier can move the target up to 10 feet from its original position.

ECOLOGY

Environment any forests (Halochthon)
Organization solitary or squad (2–8)
Treasure incidental

Frujai are sentient fungal colonies native to the toroid-shaped world of Halochthon.

Frujais are well-adapted to the planet’s constant, dramatic fluctuations of gravity, light, and temperature, and have developed both biological and psychic means of overcoming these obstacles.

In many ways, frujais function like insect colonies. The center of the colony is a massive, living hub that stands on three agile legs. It spawns dozens or even hundreds of smaller soldiers over the course of its lifetime to perform the detail work.

During the unpredictable and brutal winters, frujais hibernate, awakening during the thaw to blanket their territory in spores that infest the corpses of less fortunate creatures. If no such targets are available, the colony hunts aggressively to create a source for its spores to mature—attacking whatever living creatures it encounters.

The newly sprouted immature drones (use the statistics for a frujai soldier with the young template and without the colony guard ability) look somewhat like flightless birds. They scavenge and hunt ravenously to grow stronger; those that survive eventually become soldiers and seek a colony to join.

Frujai are surprisingly intelligent. They see themselves as caretakers of the natural order, weeding out weaker prey and maintaining ecological balance. They enjoy gathering and discussing their unique worldviews. Xenolinguists find the frujai language largely centered on abstract cycles, alien philosophies, and the joy of ravenous feasting. However, the frujais’ telepathic abilities allow them to communicate with most sentient creatures on a more practical level.
